o: U brlohu, v nějž se smeklo.
t: By the burrow into which it slipped.

o: Očko Kůži z šupin řeklo.
t: The little eye said to the Skin of scales.

o: „Slyš, co praví Očko rudé.
t: "Listen to what Red Eye says."

o: S Nagem tančili smrt bude!“
t: "With Nagu they danced — death is coming!"

o: Čelem k čelu stanem v ráz.
t: Head to head, tent in a single stroke.

o: (Vzdálenost jen dodrž, Nagu.)
t: (Just keep your distance, Nagu.)

o: Zemřít musí jeden z násl.
t: One of us must die.

o: (Dle tvojí libosti. Nagu!)
t: (As you please, Nagu!)

o: Od přemetu ku přemetu.
t: From one tumble to the next.

o: (Ukryti se spěj hned, Nagu!)
t: (Hide yourself at once, Nagu!)

o: Hal Smrt chybila se v letu –.
t: Half Death missed him as it leapt —

o: (Nyní běda tobě, Nagu!)
t: (Now woe to you, Nagu!)

o: Toto je příběh o velkém boji, jejž Riki - Tiki-Tavi probojoval samoten v koupelně velkého indického letohrádku v posádce v Segowlee.
t: This is the story of the great fight which Rikki-Tiki-Tavi fought single-handed in the bathroom of a great Indian bungalow in the cantonment at Segowlee.

o: Darzy, pták krejčík, mu pomáhal, a Čučundra, krysa pižmová, která nikdy nevkročí doprostřed síně, nýbrž pobíhá stále kolem zdi, přispěla mu svou radou; ale Riki - Tiki provedl skutečnou bitvu.
t: Darzy, the tailor bird, helped him, and Chuchundra, the musk rat, who never ventures into the middle of the hall but always scurries round the walls, gave him his advice; but Rikki-Tiki fought the real battle.

o: Byl to mungo, který podle kožichu a ocasu vyhlíží jako malá kočka, ale podle hlavy a zvyků je spíše jako lasice.
t: He was a mongoose, looking, in coat and tail, like a small cat, but in head and habits more like a weasel.

o: Oči a konec nepokojného nosíku byly růžové; mohl se drbat po těle, kdekoli chtěl, kteroukoli nohou mu napadlo, přední nebo zadní; mohl rozčepýřit ocas, až vyhlížel jako štětka k cídění lahví, a válečný pokřik jeho, chvátal-li vysokou travou, zněl: »Rik-tik-tiki– i tiki-tčk!«.
t: His eyes and the tip of his restless little snout were pink; he could scratch himself anywhere on his body with whichever of his feet he pleased, fore or hind; he could fluff up his tail until it looked like a bottle-brush, and his war cry, when he hurried through the tall grass, was: "Rik-tik-tiki — and tiki-tchik!"

o: Jednoho dne spláchl ho silný letní příval z doupěte, kde žil se svým otcem a matkou, a unášel jej, ač se vzpíral a bránil, dolů silniční strouhou.
t: One day a heavy summer shower washed him out of the hole where he lived with his father and mother, and carried him, though he struggled and resisted, down the road-side ditch.

o: Zachytil se chomáčku trávy tudy plovoucího a držel se ho pevně, až pozbyl smyslův.
t: He caught hold of a tuft of grass that was floating by and clung to it tightly until he lost his senses.

o: Když se vzpamatoval, ležel na parném výsluní uprostřed zahradní stezky věru důkladně zablácený, a malý jakýs hošík pravil: »Tu je mrtvý mungo.
t: When he came to his senses, he lay on the steaming hot ground in the middle of the garden path, thoroughly muddied, and a small boy said: "Here's a dead mongoose.

o: Vystrojíme mu pohřeb.«.
t: We'll give him a funeral."

o: »Ne,« řekla jeho matka; »vezmeme jej domů a osušíme jej.
t: "No," said his mother; "we'll take him home and dry him.

o: Snad ani není opravdu mrtev.«.
t: Maybe he isn't really dead."

o: Vzali jej do domu a nějaký velký muž pozdvihl ho ukazováčkem a palcem a pravil, že není mrtev, ale napolo udušen; zaobalili ho tedy do bavlnky a zahřívali ho, až otevřel oči a kýchl.
t: They took him into the house, and some large man lifted him up by the finger and thumb and said he wasn't dead but half suffocated; so they wrapped him in cotton wool and warmed him until he opened his eyes and sneezed.

o: »Tak,« řekl velký muž (byl to Angličan, který se právě přistěhoval do letohrádku). »Teď ho nepoplašte, uvidíme, co bude dělat.«.
t: "So," said the large man (he was an Englishman who had just moved into the summerhouse), "don't startle him now; we'll see what he does."

o: Poplašiti munga je snad tou nejtěžší věcí na světě, poněvadž je od čenichu až po ocas naplněn zvědavostí.
t: Startling a mung is perhaps the hardest thing in the world, for from his nose to his tail he is filled with curiosity.

o: Heslem celého mungova rodu je: »Běhej a hledej!« a Riki - Tiki byl pravým mungem.
t: The motto of the whole mung tribe is: "Run and seek!" And Riki-Tiki was a true mung.

o: Prohlédl bavlnku, uznal, že se nehodí k jídlu, oběhl kolem stolu, usedl a upravoval si kožíšek, poškrabal se a vyskočil hošíkovi na rameno.
t: He examined the cotton wool, decided it was not fit for eating, ran round the table, sat down and arranged his fur, scratched himself, and sprang onto the boy's shoulder.

o: »Nelekej se, Teddy,« pravil otec. »Je to jeho způsob uzavírati přátelství.«.
t: "Don't be afraid, Teddy," said the father. "That's his way of making friends."

o: »Ou, lehtá mne pod bradou!« volal Teddy.
t: "Ow, it tickles me under the chin!" cried Teddy.

o: Riki - Tiki díval se chlapci dolů za límec a za krk, očichával mu ucho a skočil opět na zem, kde usedl, mna si nos.
t: Riki-Tiki looked down the boy's collar and behind his neck, cocked his ear at him, and jumped down again to the ground, where he sat and wiped his nose.

o: »Můj bože,« řekla Teddyho matka, »a tomu se říká divoké zvíře!
t: "Good heavens," said Teddy's mother, "and they call that a wild animal!"

o: Myslím, že je proto tak krotký, že jsme k němu byli laskavi.«.
t: I think he's so tame because we were kind to him."

o: »Všichni mungové jsou takoví,« pravil její manžel. »Nebude-li ho Teddy tahat za ocas, nebo nezkusí-li ho zavírat do klece, bude běhat celý den po domě.
t: "All mungs are like that," said her husband. "If Teddy doesn't drag him by the tail, or try to shut him up in a cage, he'll be running about the house all day."

o: Dejte mu něco jíst.«.
t: Give him something to eat."

o: Dali mu kus syrového masa.
t: They gave him a piece of raw meat.

o: Riki - Tikimu chutnalo velice, a když ho snědl, vyběhl na verandu, usedl na slunci a rozčechrával si kožich, aby mu proschmil až do kořínkův.
t: Riki-Tiki found it very tasty, and when he had eaten it he ran out onto the veranda, sat down in the sun and ruffled his fur to dry it through to the roots.

o: Pak mu již bylo lépe.
t: After that he felt better.

o: »Zde v domě a kolem komu,« pravil k sobě, »je více věcí, jež možno vyzvědět, než viděla celá moje rodina za celý svůj život.
t: "Here in the house and around it," he said to himself, "there are more things to be found out than my whole family saw in all its life."

o: Zůstanu zde najisto a vyzvím všechno.«.
t: I'll stay here for sure and find out everything."

o: Ztrávil celý den čenichaje a slídě.
t: He spent the whole day sniffing and prowling about.

o: V koupelně byl by se málem utopil ve vědru; strčil nos do inkoustu na psacím stole a pak si ho spálil o konec doutníku velkého muže, jelikož mu skočil na klín, aby viděl, jak se píše.
t: In the bathroom he would have drowned himself in the tub; he poked his nose into the ink on the writing table and then burned it on the end of the large man's cigar, since he had jumped onto his knee to see how writing was done.

o: V podvečer běžel do ložnice Teddyho, aby viděl, jak se rozsvěcují kerosenové lampy, a když Teddy vlezl do postele, Riki - Tiki tam vylezl též.
t: In the evening he ran into Teddy's bedroom to see how the kerosene lamps were lit, and when Teddy climbed into bed, Riki-Tiki climbed up there too.

o: Byl však neklidným soudruhem, jelikož musil dávat pozor na každý ruch a šustot po celou noc, a musel vědět, kdo ho dělá.
t: But he was a restless fellow, for he had to keep watch on every sound and rustle all through the night, and he had to know who was making it.

o: Teddyho matka a otec přišli se naposled podívat na svého hošíka, a Riki - Tiki hleděl na ně s polštáře. »To nevidím ráda,« řekla matka Teddyho; »mohl by dítě kousnout.«.
t: Teddy's mother and father came to have one last look at their little man, and Riki-Tiki watched them from the pillow. "I don't like that," said Teddy's mother; "he might bite the child."

o: »Neudělá nic takového,« pravil otec. »Teddy je bezpečnější s tímto zvířátkem, než kdyby tu měl hafana, který by ho hlídal.
t: "He wouldn't do anything like that," said the father. "Teddy is safer with this little beast than if he had a mongrel dog here to guard him."

o: Kdyby teď vešel had do ložnice –«.
t: "If only a snake were to come into the bedroom now—"

o: Ale matka Teddyho nechtěla na něco tak hrozného ani pomyslit.
t: But Teddy's mother wouldn't even think of anything so dreadful.

o: Záhy z rána přišel Riki - Tiki k snídaní na verandu, sedě Teddymu na rameně, a dali mu banány a vařená vejce; a on jim sedal všem po řadě na klínech, protože každý dobře vychovaný mungo pomýšlí vždy na to, aby se stal jednou domácím mungem a měl pokoje k probíhání.
t: Early in the morning Riki-Tiki came to breakfast on the veranda, sitting on Teddy's shoulder, and they gave him bananas and boiled eggs; and he sat on each of their knees in turn, for every well-bred mongoose always thinks of becoming one day a house mongoose with rooms to run about in.

o: Matka Riki - Tikiho žila kdys v domě generálově v Segowlee a vštípila Rikimu důkladně, jak si má počínat, setká-li se s bílými lidmi.
t: Riki-Tiki's mother had lived once in the General's house at Segowlee and had thoroughly instilled in Riki how he was to behave when he met white people.

o: Na to odběhl Riki - Tiki do zahrady, aby shlédl, co tu bude k shlédnutí.
t: At that Riki-Tiki ran off into the garden to see what there was to be seen.

o: Byla to velká zahrada, jen do polovice kultivovaná, s keři růží »Maréchal Niels«, velkými jako besídky, s citrónovými a oranžovými stromy, s bambusovými houštinami a vysokou travou.
t: It was a big garden, cultivated only halfway, with rose bushes of "Maréchal Niels" as large as arbours, with lemon and orange trees, with bamboo thickets and tall grass.

o: Riki - Tiki si olizoval rty. »To je skvostné místečko pro lov,« řekl si, a ocas se mu rozčepýřil jako štětka již při pouhém pomyšlení.
t: Riki-Tiki licked his lips. "A fine place for hunting," he said to himself, and his tail bristled like a brush at the very thought.

o: Probíhal zahradou nahoru i dolů, čenichal tu i tam, až zaslechl velmi žalostné hlasy z trnitého keře.
t: He ran up and down the garden, nosing here and there, until he heard very plaintive voices from a thorny bush.

o: Byl to Darzy, krejčík, a jeho žena.
t: It was Darzy, the tailor, and his wife.

o: Udělali si krásné hnízdečko ze dvou velkých listů, které přitáhli dohromady a sešili na okrajích vlákny, a vyplnili Vnitřek bavlnkou a měkkým prachovým peřím.
t: They had made a lovely little nest of two big leaves, which they had pulled together and stitched at the edges with threads, and filled the inside with cotton and soft downy feathers.

o: Hnízdo se houpalo semo tamo, a oni seděli na jeho okraji a naříkali.
t: The nest rocked to and fro, and they sat on its edge and wailed.

o: »Co je vám?« ptal se Riki - Tiki.
t: "What's the matter with you?" asked Riki-Tiki.

o: »Jsme velmi nešťastni,« odpověděl Darzy. »Jedno naše mládě vypadlo včera z hnízda a Nag je snědl.«.
t: "We are very unhappy," answered Darzy. "One of our young ones fell out of the nest yesterday, and Nag ate it."

o: »Hm!« pravil Riki - Tiki, »to je velmi smutné.
t: "Hm!" said Riki-Tiki, "that's very sad.

o: Avšak jsem zde cizincem. Kdo je to Nag?«.
t: But I am a stranger here. Who is Nag?"

o: Darzy a jeho žena jen se přikrčili do hnízda a neodpověděli; neboť z husté slámy pod křovím ozval se tlumený sykot – strašlivý mrazivý zvuk, tak že Riki - Tiki až odskočil na dvě stopy na zad.
t: Darzy and his wife only shrank back into the nest and did not answer; for out of the thick straw under the bushes came a muffled hiss—a terrible, chilling sound, so that Riki-Tiki jumped back two feet onto his hind legs.

o: Na to kousek po kousku vylézala z trávy hlava a rozepiatý klobouk Nagův, velkého černého brejlovce, dlouhého pět stop od hlavy až k ocasu.
t: Then, bit by bit, a head and Nag's spread hood rose out of the grass, Nag the great black cobra, five feet long from head to tail.

o: Pozdvihl třetinu svého těla od země a stál tu kývaje se se strany na stranu, jako se houpe pampeliška ve větru, a díval se na Riki - Tikiho zlomyslným hadím okem, které nikdy nemění svého výrazu, nechť si myslí had cokoli.
t: He lifted a third of his body off the ground and stood there swaying from side to side, as a dandelion sways in the wind, and looked at Riki-Tiki with his sly snake's eye, which never changes its expression, let the snake think whatever it likes.

o: »Kdo je Nag?« syčel. »Já jsem Nag.
t: "Who is Nag?" he hissed. "I am Nag."

o: Vznešený bůh Brahma vtiskl celému našemu rodu své znamení, jelikož první brejlovec– rozestřel svůj klobouk nad Brahmou, aby ho ve spánku chránil před sluncem. Viz a třes se!«.
t: "The exalted god Brahma imprinted his sign upon our whole race, since the first goggle-eyed one spread his hat over Brahma to shield him in sleep from the sun. Look and tremble!"

o: Rozepial svůj klobouk šíře než kdy jindy, a tu uzřel Riki - Tiki na zadní straně jeho znamení brejlí, jež vypadá zrovna tak jako obroučky brejlí.
t: He spread his hat wider than ever before, and there he saw Riki-Tiki on the reverse side of his sign of the goggles, which looks exactly like the rims of spectacles.

o: Zděsil se na chvíli; ale mungovi je nemožno býti zděšenu delší dobu.
t: He was dismayed for a moment; but a mung cannot be dismayed for long.

o: Ačkoli Riki - Tiki nikdy dřív neviděl živého brejlovce, krmila ho přec jeho matka mrtvými hady, a věděl, že je životním povoláním dospělého munga bojovat z hady a požírat je.
t: Although Riki-Tiki had never before seen a living goggle-eyed one, his mother had fed him dead snakes, and he knew that it was the calling of an adult mung to fight snakes and devour them.

o: Nag to věděl též a na dně svého chladného srdce byl uděšen.
t: Nag knew this too, and at the bottom of his cold heart he was dismayed.

o: »Nu,« pravil Riki - Tiki, a ocas se mu začal zase čepýřit, »znamení nebo neznamení, ale myslíš, že je v pořádku požírat holátka vypadlá z hnízda?«.
t: "Well," said Riki-Tiki, and his tail began to bristle again, "sign or no sign, but do you think it is all right to eat fledglings fallen from the nest?"

o: Nag přemýšlel a dával pozor na každý nejmenší pohyb v trávě za Riki - Tikim.
t: Nag pondered and watched every slightest movement in the grass behind Riki-Tiki.

o: Věděl, že mungové v zahradě znamenají pro něho a jeho rodinu smrt dříve či později, a snažil se tedy odvrátiti pozornost Riki - Tikiho k neopatrnosti.
t: He knew that mungs in the garden meant death for him and his family sooner or later, and so he tried to turn Riki-Tiki's attention to carelessness.

o: Sehnul tedy poněkud hlavu a naklonil ji stranou.
t: So he bowed his head somewhat and tilted it to one side.

o: »Promluvme si o tom,« pravil. »Ty pojídáš vejce.
t: "Let us talk about that," he said. "You eat eggs."

o: Proč bych já neměl pojídat ptákův?«.
t: "Why shouldn't I eat birds?"

o: »Za sebe! Ohlédni se za sebe!« zazpíval Darzy.
t: "Behind you! Look behind you!" sang Darzy.

o: Riki - Tiki byl příliš chytrý, než aby mařil čas ohlížením.
t: Riki-Tiki was too clever to waste time looking back.

o: Vyskočil, jak vysoko mohl, a těsně pod ním projela hlava Nagainy, Nagovy zlé ženy.
t: He sprang up as high as he could, and just below him passed the head of Nagaina, Nag's evil wife.

o: Připlazila se za ním, dokud hovořil, aby jej usmrtila; slyšel její zuřivý sykot, když se její rána minula s cílem.
t: She crept up behind him while he spoke, to kill him; he heard her furious hiss when her strike missed its mark.

o: Riki dopadl skorém na její záda, a kdyby byl býval starým mungem, byl by věděl, že nyní byl čas zlomiti jí vaz jediným kousnutím; ale bál se hrozného, bičovitého zpětného kousnutí hadova.
t: Riki fell almost upon her back, and had he been an old mung, he would have known that now was the time to break her neck with a single bite; but he feared the terrible, whip-like backward strike of the snake.

o: Zakousl se sice opravdu do něho, ale ne na dlouho, a odskočil od mrskajícího sebou ocasu hadího, zanechávaje Nagainu raněnou a rozzuřenou.
t: He did indeed bite into her, but not for long, and he sprang away from the snake's thrashing tail, leaving Nagaina wounded and enraged.

o: »Zlý, zlý Darzy!« volal Nag, vymršťuje se jak vysoko mohl, aby dosáhl hnízda v trnitém křoví; ale Darzy je udělal mimo dosah hadí, a ono jen se houpalo semo tamo.
t: "Bad, bad Darzy!" cried Nag, throwing himself up as high as he could to reach the nest in the thorny bush; but Darzy had put it out of the snakes' reach, and it only swung to and fro.

o: Riki - Tiki cítil, že mu oči rudnou a zapalují se (zčervenají-li mungovi oči, je rozzloben).
t: Riki-Tiki felt his eyes reddening and glowing (when a mongoose's eyes redden, he is angry).

o: Posadil se na ocas a na zadní nohy jako malý klokan a rozhlížel se kolem třesa se zlostí.
t: He sat down on his tail and hind legs like a little kangaroo and looked around, trembling with rage.

o: Ale Nag s Nagainou zmizeli v trávě.
t: But Nag and Nagaina had vanished into the grass.

o: Nepodaří-li se hadu jeho útok, nedá nikdy na jevo, co zamýšlí učiniti v nejbližší době.
t: If a snake's attack fails, it never shows what it intends to do in the near future.

o: Riki - Tiki nedbal o to, aby je následoval, jelikož si nebyl jist, zmohl-li by dva hady zároveň.
t: Riki-Tiki did not care about following them, since he was not sure he could cope with two snakes at once.

o: Odcupal tedy na stezku pískem posypanou u domu a usedl, přemýšleje.
t: So he hopped onto the sandy path near the house and sat down, thinking.

o: Byla to pro něho vážná věc.
t: It was a serious matter for him.

o: Čtete-li staré přírodopisné knihy, dočtete se v nich, že zápasí-li mungo s hadem a kousne-li ho had, že doběhne pro jistou bylinku, která jej uzdraví.
t: If you read old natural history books, you will find in them that when a mongoose fights with a snake and the snake bites it, the mongoose runs off for a certain herb that will heal him.

o: To není pravda.
t: That is not true.

o: Vítězství záleží jediné na bystrosti oka a rychlosti nohou, – hadí uštknutí proti mungovu skoku – a jelikož nemůže žádné oko sledovati pohyb útočící hadí hlavy při ráně, je věc tím jen ještě podivuhodnější než kterákoli kouzelná bylinka.
t: Victory depends solely on the quickness of the eye and the speed of the feet — the snake's strike against the mongoose's leap — and since no eye can follow the movement of the attacking snake's head at the moment of the strike, the matter is all the more marvellous than any magic herb.

o: Riki - Tiki věděl, že je mladým mungem, a těšilo ho tedy tím více, pomyslil-li, že se mu podařilo odolati útoku ze zadu.
t: Riki-Tiki knew that he was a young mongoose, and it pleased him all the more when he thought that he had managed to withstand an attack from behind.

o: Dodalo mu to sebedůvěry, a když k němu přiběhl Teddy po stezičce, byl Riki - Tiki zcela ochoten k mazlení.
t: That gave him confidence, and when Teddy came running up the little path, Riki-Tiki was quite ready for fondling.

o: Avšak právě, když byl Teddy sehnut, zavrtělo sebou něco v prachu a jemný hlásek řekl: »Pozor!
t: But just as Teddy was bending down, something stirred in the dust and a thin little voice said: "Look out!

o: Jsem Smrt!« byl to Karait, šedě hnědý hádek, který nejraději lehává v prachu cest; uštknutí jeho je právě tak nebezpečné, jako brejlovcovo.
t: I am Death!" It was Karait, the grey-brown little snake who loves best to lie in the dust of the path; his strike is just as dangerous as a cobra's.

o: Ale je tak malý, že si ho nikdo nepovšimne a tak může lidem tím spíše ublížiti.
t: But he is so small that nobody notices him, and so he can do people harm all the more easily.

o: Riki - Tikiho oči opět zrudly a tančil směrem ku Karaitovi oním zvláštním houpavým a kolébavým chodem, který je vlastním jeho rodu.
t: Riki-Tiki's eyes reddened again, and he danced toward Karait with that peculiar waddling, rocking gait peculiar to his kind.

o: Vyhlíží to velice směšně, ale je to tak dokonale vy-rovnovážený krok, že z něho lze odskočiti rychle do kterého úhlu chce; v boji s hady je to velkou výhodou.
t: It looks very funny, but it is such a perfectly balanced step that he can spring off from it quickly in whatever direction he wishes; in a fight with snakes that is a great advantage.

o: Riki - Tiki ani nevěděl, že podniká mnohem nebezpečnější věc, než je boj s Nagem, neboť Karait je tak malý a umí se tak otáčeti, že kdyby se mu Riki - Tiki nezakousl do těla těsně za hlavu, obrátil by se ještě a uštknul by ho do čenichu nebo oka.
t: Riki-Tiki did not even know that he was undertaking something far more dangerous than a fight with Nag, for Karait is so small and can turn about so deftly that, had Riki-Tiki not bitten him in the body just behind the head, the snake would have turned again and struck him in the muzzle or the eye.

t: But Riki-Tiki did not know that: his eyes were all reddened, and he rocked forward and back, looking out for a suitable spot to bite.

o: Karait se vymrštil, Riki - Tiki uskočil stranou a chystal se běžeti na něj, ale zlá, malá, prachově šedá hlava mrskla sebou o čárku mimo jeho šíji; musil přeskočiti tělo a hlava zas se mu mihla těsně u nohou.
t: Karait sprang up, Riki-Tiki jumped aside and prepared to rush at him, but the evil little dusty-grey head darted past beyond his neck; he had to leap over the body, and the head flashed again close by his feet.

t: The bite numbed Karait, and Riki-Tiki was just preparing to devour him from tail to head, as was the family custom at dinner, when it occurred to him that a full stomach makes a mongoose lazy, and if he wanted to keep all his sharpness and strength, he had to stay slim.

o: Riki - Tikiho bavil veškerý ten poplach, kterého ovšem nechápal.
t: Riki-Tiki was highly diverted by all the commotion, though of course he did not understand it.

o: Riki - Tiki byl úplně spokojen sám s sebou.
t: Riki-Tiki was perfectly satisfied with himself.

o: Toho večera procházel se při večeři po stole, mezi sklenicemi a vínem a byl by se mohl třikráte nasytiti všelikými dobrými věcmi.
t: That evening he prowled about the table during dinner, among the glasses and the wine, and could have stuffed himself three times over with all manner of good things.

o: Připomínal si však Naga a Nagainu, a ačkoli bylo velice příjemno, hladila-li ho a laskala Teddyho matka a seděl-li Teddymu na rameně, zčervenaly mu přece chvílemi oči a vyrážel ze sebe svůj dlouhý válečný pokřik: »R i k-t i k–t i k i–t i k i–t č k!«.
t: Yet he remembered Naga and Nagaina, and although it was very pleasant when Teddy's mother stroked and fondled him and he sat on Teddy's shoulder, his eyes would still redden at times, and he would burst out with his long war cry: "R i k-t i k–t i k i–t i k i–t č k!"

o: Teddy si ho odnesl s sebou do postele a chtěl, aby mu Riki - Tiki spal pod bradou.
t: Teddy took him along to bed and wanted Riki-Tiki to sleep under his chin.

o: Riki - Tiki byl příliš dobře vychován, aby byl kousal nebo škrábal, ale jakmile Teddy usnul, vybral se na svou noční procházku kolem domu; po tmě narazil na Čučundru, krysu pižmovou, která pobíhala kolem zdi.
t: Riki-Tiki was too well brought up to bite or scratch, but as soon as Teddy fell asleep he set out on his nightly round around the house; in the dark he ran into Chuchundra, the musk rat, who was scurrying about along the wall.

o: Čučundra je velice bázlivé zvířátko.

o: »Nezabíjej mne,« pravila Čučundra skorém plačky. »Riki -Tiki, nezabíjej mne!«.
t: "Don't kill me," said Chuchundra in a voice of bitter weeping. "Riki-Tiki, don't kill me!"

t: "What do you mean, a snake-killer killing musk rats?" said Riki-Tiki scornfully.

t: "He who kills snakes may himself be killed by snakes," said Chuchundra more carefully than before. "And who assures me that Nag won't mistake me for you on some dark night?"

o: »O to není nejmenší starost,« ušklíbl se Riki -Tiki; »ale Nag je v zahradě, a vím, že ty tam nejdeš.«.
t: "Don't worry about that," grinned Riki-Tiki; "but Nag is in the garden, and I know that you don't go there."

o: »Můj bratranec Chua, krysa polní, vyprávěl mi –« pravila Čučundra, ale v tom se zarazila. »Co ti vyprávěl?«.
t: "My cousin Chua, the field rat, told me—" said Chuchundra, but there she stopped. "What did he tell you?"

o: »Pst! Nag je všude, Riki - Tiki.

t: Čučundra sat down and wept, tears running down his whiskers. "I'm a poor wretch," he sighed. "I never had enough courage to run out into the middle of the room."

o: Pst! Nemusím ti již nic povídat.

t: "Everything. Have we had any munga in the garden so far?"

t: If the house is empty, we are the king and queen of the garden; and remember that as soon as our eggs in the melon bed hatch, which may happen as early as tomorrow – our children will need space and quiet!"

t: Nag was asleep, and Rikki-Tikki, gazing at his great back, pondered in which spot he might bite most securely. t: "It must be the head," he said at last; "the head just above the hood; and once I have hold of it, I must not let go."

t: The snake's head lay a little to one side of the tub, under the belly of the vessel; and when Rikki clenched his teeth, he braced his back against the red earthenware pot, so that he could press the snake's head to the ground.

o: A pak bylo jím třepáno sem a tam, jako když pes třepe chycenou krysou – sem a tam po podlaze, nahoru a dolů – a kolem dokola ve velkých kruzích; ale Riki měl zrudlé oči a držel se pevně, jak sebou hadovo tělo smýkalo a švihalo po podlaze, shazujíc cínovou naběračku a misku na mýdlo a umývači kartáč, a bilo sebou o cínové boky vany.
t: And then he was shaken to and fro, as when a dog shakes a caught rat — to and fro over the floor, up and down — and round and about in great circles; but Rikki had reddened eyes and held fast, as the snake's body writhed and lashed over the floor, knocking down a tin ladle and a soap dish and a scrubbing brush, and beating against the tin sides of the bath.

o: Drže se pevně, svíral čelisti pevněji a pevněji, bylt jist, že bude utlučen do smrti a pro rodinnou čest byl rozhodnut dáti se nalézt s čelistmi zaťatými.
t: Hold on tight, he clenched his jaws tighter and tighter, certain that he would be beaten to death, and for the honour of his family he was determined to be found with his jaws locked.

t: His head was spinning, faintness came over him, his whole body ached, he felt as though he had been smashed into tiny pieces, when suddenly something went off like a thunderclap, right behind him; a searing wind drove the last of his consciousness out of him and a red fire singed his fur.

t: The big man was awakened by the din in the bathroom and fired both barrels of his shotgun at Naga right under his hat.

t: Riki-Tiki held on, his eyes closed; he was now quite certain that he himself was dead; but the cobra's head no longer moved, and the big man lifted it up and said.

t: "It is our mongoose again, Alice; the little fellow has saved our life this time."

o: A Teddyho matka vešla se zbělelou tváří a viděla, co zbylo z Naga, a Riki - Tiki se odvlekl do Teddyho ložnice a ztrávil polovinu noci tím, že se něžně protřepával po celém těle, aby se přesvědčil, je-li opravdu rozbit na padesát kusů jak se mu zdálo.
t: And Teddy's mother came in with a blanched face and saw what was left of Naga, and Riki-Tiki dragged himself into Teddy's bedroom and spent half the night gently shaking himself all over to convince himself that he really was broken into fifty pieces, as it seemed to him.

t: When morning finally dawned, Riki-Tiki was all stiff, but he was very well satisfied with himself and with his deeds. "Now I still have to settle accounts with Nagaina, and that will be worse than five Nagas, and nobody can know when the eggs she spoke of will hatch."
